pairs.subject: streaming-output
pairs.evidence: src/app/api/events/stream/route.ts:142 The SSE proxy drains the upstream reader inside start() and enqueues every chunk without checking controller.desiredSize, so a pull-based upstream that could be slowed instead fills an unbounded queue whenever the browser reads slowly. Downstream, the live log is capped only by entry count (MAX_EVENTS_BUFFER = 1_000 in src/stores/eventStore.ts:26) and evicts at :341-344 without saying so, so the bound is in one currency and the truncation is silent.

techniques.evidence: src/app/api/events/stream/route.ts:142 The read loop in start() ignores desiredSize, which is the 'unbounded intermediate queue' the technique forbids; a pull() source would keep backpressure. The client ring (eventStore.ts:26/341) has an entry budget but no byte budget, and its head eviction records no count or notice.

src/hooks/useEventStream.ts:117 EventSource does the framing and personaEventWire.ts parses a typed, field-validated payload, which is good. But only the named 'event' type is subscribed, so unknown event types are dropped instead of forwarded, and off-contract frames are thrown away at :118-121 with no counter, sample or diagnostic event.

src/hooks/useEventStream.ts:121 Every SSE message calls appendEvent straight away, a separate zustand set and a new array each time (eventStore.ts:333-348). The list, the bus and the counts re-render once per arrival; there is no coalesced flush on a set cadence.

src/app/api/events/stream/route.ts:137 A client abort cancels the upstream reader. Abort, upstream done and upstream error all reach the one finally block (:147-155), which clears the heartbeat, removes the listener and closes the controller exactly once. An upstream error closes the stream cleanly, but EventSource treats any close as an error and reconnects, so the client still shows 'reconnecting' rather than claiming success.

src/stores/eventStore.ts:334 An event-bus tail has no runs to tell apart; events are keyed and deduplicated by id. The consumer-lifecycle half is covered by the per-effect 'disposed' flag and closing the previous EventSource before reconnecting (useEventStream.ts:103-110).
src/components/dashboard/views/events/index.tsx:49 The only user input on this page publishes a fresh bus event. Nothing interjects into an in-flight turn.
src/components/dashboard/EventsListPanel.tsx:31 The only sink is a React table that is re-rendered with rows repainted in place, so there is no append-only surface whose commit has to be decided.

pairs.registryProposal: This subject assumes a 'run' with a terminal outcome. A perpetual monitoring tail (an event-bus SSE feed) has no run identity, no phase and no settled record, yet buffering, parsing and throttling still apply in full. The golden path could name 'perpetual live tail' as a variant in which run-attribution, phase-derivation and finalization outcomes reduce to connection-lifecycle concerns.
